title: How to Create Responsive Websites
summary: Overview of the four main ways to make a page respond to screen width: media queries, CSS Grid, Flexbox and the Bootstrap framework. Each gets a short demo; Grid, Flexbox and Bootstrap are previewed ahead of their own sections, and the lesson ends by suggesting you experiment with the provided demo files.

concepts.heading: What 'responsive' means
points: Pages must look right on desktops, laptops, tablets and phones, so the layout has to adapt to the viewport width.
Try resizing a real site's window: navigation items collapse into a menu at some width, and a search box may vanish on narrow screens. Those switch-over widths are breakpoints.
Four techniques: media queries, CSS Grid, Flexbox, and an external framework such as Bootstrap. There is no single best one; they are tools with different strengths.

concepts.heading: 1. Media queries
points: Written where a selector would go, starting with @media followed by a condition in parentheses, then a block of normal rules.
@media (max-width: 600px) { ... } applies the inner rules whenever the viewport is 600px wide or narrower.
Different widths and different rule sets can be defined, one block per breakpoint. Detailed in the next lesson.

concepts.heading: 2. CSS Grid (2D layout)
points: Put display: grid on a container; its direct children become grid items.
grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr defines two equal columns. fr is a fraction of the available space.
grid-template-rows: 100px 200px 200px defines three rows with fixed heights (rows are often given in px).
gap: 30px sets spacing between rows and columns.
grid-column: span 2 on one item (class .first) makes it cover both columns, producing a wide header-like cell.
Example uses a container div with five .card children. Described as flexible for complex layouts with only a few lines. A whole section follows.

concepts.heading: 3. Flexbox (1D layout)
points: Flexbox lays items along one axis, either a row or a column. Put display: flex on the container.
flex: 1 on each child gives all children equal share of the width. flex: 2 makes a child twice as wide as a flex: 1 sibling; flex: 0.5 makes it half as wide.
Sizes are ratios, not pixels, so they scale with the container automatically. In a vertical flexbox the same ratios divide the height (for example header 1, main 3, footer 1 = 5 parts).
Demo has four cards with a fixed height of 100px; the first gets flex 2, the second flex 0.5.

concepts.heading: 4. Bootstrap framework
points: A framework is external CSS (and JS) brought into the page; it defines many ready-made class names such as card, row, container.
Loaded through a link tag to its stylesheet CDN; adding class names applies rounded corners, fonts and layout without writing the CSS.
Its grid is built on Flexbox and divides the width into 12 columns. col-6 spans 6 of 12 (50%), col-2 spans 2, col-4 spans 4; 6+2+4 = 12 fills the row.
Widths are percentages, so col-6 is 500px in a 1000px container and 1000px in 2000px.

concepts.heading: Choosing a method
points: Because each technique is suited to different jobs, learn all of them and mix as needed; later sections cover Grid, Flexbox and Bootstrap in depth.
(Extra) In real projects they are combined, for example Flexbox for a nav bar, Grid for the page, media queries for tweaks at breakpoints.

task.name: Explore the four responsiveness demos
task.starting_point: Download '8.2 Responsiveness'. index.html links to media-query.html, grid.html, flexbox.html and bootstrap.html.
task.goal: Open each demo, resize the preview and tweak values to see how each technique reacts. No fixed solution.
steps: Open index.html in the preview and follow the links.
In media-query.html change the 600px breakpoint and the sizes.
In grid.html, change the column fractions, row heights, gap and the span.
In flexbox.html, change flex values on .first and .second.
In bootstrap.html, change the col-N numbers (keep a row to 12 total) and resize the window.
task.expected_result: Familiarity with how each technique rescales the layout; nothing to submit.

pitfalls: Using fixed px widths for everything, so layouts cannot adapt.
(Extra) Forgetting the viewport meta tag, which stops media queries behaving properly on phones.
(Extra) Repo demo files carry an author footer; ignore it.

playground.coverage: Covers the viewport meta tag, a fixed vs fluid width demo and a list of the four techniques with pointers to later sections. Tasks make cards fluid with percentage widths.
gaps_and_ideas: Add small live side-by-side demos of the four methods (media query, grid with 1fr 1fr and span 2, flex 2/0.5/1/1, Bootstrap col-6/2/4) that the user can resize, as the lecture does.
Add the 12-column arithmetic as a mini quiz (which col-N values fill a row).
Add a task to find a real site's breakpoint by resizing the window.
